result.summary: Apollodorus begins with Sky as first ruler, his children by Earth, and his overthrow by Cronus. Cronus then swallows his own children until Rhea hides the infant Zeus in Crete and tricks Cronus with a stone.

scenes.title: Sky's Rule and Imprisoned Children
scenes.summary: Sky weds Earth and fathers the Hundred-handed and the Cyclopes, then binds them in Tartarus.

scenes.title: Titans Overthrow Sky
scenes.summary: Earth bears the Titans and Titanides, then urges the Titans to attack Sky. Cronus mutilates Sky, Furies are born, and Cronus becomes ruler.
scenes.stakes: Sky stands to lose his throne and his power over the world.

scenes.title: Cronus Swallows His Children
scenes.summary: Cronus re-imprisons his brothers, weds Rhea, and swallows his children to avoid a prophesied overthrow.
scenes.stakes: Cronus fears losing his throne to his own son; his children are swallowed.

scenes.title: Zeus Born in Crete
scenes.summary: Rhea gives birth to Zeus in a cave on Dicte and has him nursed and guarded. She gives Cronus a stone to swallow instead.
scenes.stakes: The infant Zeus would be swallowed if Cronus discovered him.

notable_quotes.reason: The famous trick of the swaddled stone that saves the infant Zeus.

analysis.text: Power passes violently from father to son, each ruler fearing and then falling to his offspring. This succession myth sets up Zeus's eventual rule.
Apollodorus' Library is a handbook of Greek myth, compiling older sources like Hesiod's Theogony into a prose genealogy.

legacy.text: The castration of Uranus and the swallowing of children by Cronus became standard images in art, notably Goya's Saturn Devouring His Son (c. 1820s), using the Roman name Saturn.

fun_facts.text: The Library was long attributed to Apollodorus of Athens but is now thought to date from the first or second century AD.

language_notes.text: "To wit" is an old legal phrase meaning "that is to say" or "namely."
Tartarus is the deepest part of the underworld, used as a prison for defeated or feared beings.
"Adamantine" means made of adamant, a mythical unbreakable metal.
"Big with Zeus" means pregnant with Zeus; "repaired" here means went.
"In arms" means armed, wearing weapons and armor.

context_notes.text: The Titans were the older generation of gods; the Titanides are their sisters. Cronus later rules them until Zeus overthrows him.
The Furies (Erinyes) were goddesses who punished crimes, especially murder and offenses against family.
The Curetes were divine attendants or young warriors associated with Crete who protected the infant Zeus.

literary_notes.text: The distance of Tartarus is conveyed by comparing earth-to-Tartarus with earth-to-sky, giving a sense of vast depth.
Cronus tries to avoid the prophecy by swallowing his children, and his own cruelty prepares the downfall he fears.
The substituted stone signals that Cronus's trick will be turned against him and that Zeus will survive to overthrow him.
